INSIDE THE Delhi Police's old se-
curity unit at Central Delhi's

sorts for vehicles used by the

has leamt.

The two vehicles were de-
ployed in the security unit before

lice source said, adding, “They
are now ready for auction after
receiving necessary permission
from the respective courts —
Patiala and Saket.”
Besides being in bad shape
due to the accidents, the twocars
have long surpassed their oper-

ational tenure of six-and-a-half

kilometres or six-and-a-half

One of the cars was bought

After they became defunct, the

fore being brought to the secu-
rity wing during court hearings.

articles.text:
INSIDE THE Delhi Police's old security unit at Central Delhi's Vinay Marg is a graveyard of sorts for vehicles used by the forceover the years. Inthecrowd of rusted cars are Delhi Police's last two Ambassadors which, after years of lying idle, are set to be auctioned, The Indian Express has leamt.

The two vehicles were deployed in the security unit before they were damaged in separate accidents at Mandir Marg and Delhi Cantonment in earty 2000. One ofthe accidents had claimed the lifeofa Delhi Police officer. Due to court hearingsand legal procedures, the auction of both vehicleswas delayed, a police source said, adding, "They are now ready for auction after receiving necessary permission from the respective courts - Patiala and Saket." Besides being in bad shape due to the accidents, the twocars have long surpassed their operational tenure of six-and-a-half years. The lifespan ofa petrol- or diesel-run four-wheeler in the Delhi Police is either 1.5 lakh kilometres or six-and-a-half years, whichever comes first, a police officer said. One of the cars was bought for Rs 153 lakh in 1994, andthe other for Rs 3.20 lakhin 1999, After they became defunct, the vehicles were stationed at Mandir Marg and Delhi Cantonment police stations, before being brought to the security wing during court hearings.
